page.metaTitle: Federal Policy and Regulatory Tracking | WebMonitor.fyi
page.metaDescription: Track Federal Register, Regulations.gov, congressional activity, and agency rulemaking with automated email alerts.
page.subtitle: Track the Federal Register, Regulations.gov dockets, congressional activity, and agency-specific rulemaking from one dashboard.
page.intro: Government affairs teams, lobbyists, compliance officers, and journalists need awareness across the federal policy surface: Federal Register publications, Regulations.gov dockets, congressional activity, and agency-specific rule pages. WebMonitor.fyi automates the polling layer — with hourly checks on Pro, alerts land within hours of publication.

setup.title: Map the agencies and dockets that matter
setup.body: For a financial services firm: SEC, FINRA, OCC, CFTC, FDIC. For healthcare: FDA, HHS-OCR, CMS, NIH. For energy: EPA, DOE, FERC.

setup.title: Monitor the Federal Register search URL
setup.body: A filtered search by topic or agency narrows to relevant publications. Monitor the search URL instead of the unfiltered homepage.

setup.title: Add congressional tracker pages
setup.body: Congress.gov bill-tracker URLs and committee schedule pages.

setup.title: Route alerts to the policy team's workflow
setup.body: Slack channel for team awareness; email for the dockets that need individual follow-up.

examples: Government affairs teams at corporations and trade associations
Policy researchers at think tanks and academic institutions
page.limits: Federal policy monitoring catches what each portal publishes publicly. Pre-publication drafts, agency-internal deliberations, and embargoed materials are outside scope. For Capitol Hill intelligence (member meetings, draft amendments), a different mode of monitoring is required.

faq.q: Can I track a specific Regulations.gov docket for new comments?
faq.a: Yes. The docket URL works as a monitor source. Set the criterion to "alert me on any new comment" during open comment windows.

faq.q: How does this compare to E&E News or Politico Pro?
faq.a: Those are editorial platforms with analyst coverage. WebMonitor is the alerting layer — typically used alongside them rather than as a replacement.

faq.q: Can I track bills moving through Congress?
faq.a: Yes. Congress.gov has trackable URLs per bill. Monitor catches status changes (introduction, committee referral, floor action, signature).
